screens.title: Production of Synthetic Hormones
screens.html:
Production of Synthetic Hormones

Revolutionising Medicine Through Recombinant DNA Technology

screens.title: A Life-Changing Invention
screens.html:
🔑

A Life-Changing Invention

Imagine living in a world where a diagnosis of Type 1 Diabetes was effectively a death sentence. Before 1922, there was no treatment.

Today, biotechnology allows us to 'farm' human hormones using bacteria. But how do we turn a microscopic organism into a high-tech factory?

Key point

Synthetic hormones are bio-identical to those produced in the human body, reducing the risk of immune rejection.

screens.title: Recap: Recombinant DNA Stages
screens.html:
QUICK REVIEW

Recap: Recombinant DNA Stages

Isolation

Restriction enzymes cut the target gene and plasmid, creating sticky ends.

Insertion

DNA ligase 'glues' the human gene into the bacterial plasmid.

Transformation

The recombinant plasmid is inserted into a host bacterial cell.

screens.title: Bio-factories for the Endocrine System
screens.html:
🔍

Bio-factories for the Endocrine System

Endocrine dysfunction occurs when glands produce too much or too little of a hormone.

Biotechnology provides a solution by creating synthetic hormones to replace missing ones, specifically targeting conditions like Diabetes Mellitus (insulin) and Hypothyroidism (thyroxine).

Example

Human Growth Hormone (hGH) is produced for children with growth deficiencies, preventing dwarfism.

screens.title: Synthetic Insulin Production
screens.html:
Synthetic Insulin Production

Insulin is a protein consisting of two chains (A and B). In biotechnology, these chains are often produced separately in E. coli bacteria and then combined chemically.

screens.title: Animal vs. Synthetic Insulin
screens.html:
Animal vs. Synthetic Insulin

Prior to the 1980s, insulin was extracted from the pancreases of slaughtered cows and pigs. While life-saving, it wasn't perfect.

Allergic Reactions

Slight differences in amino acid sequences caused immune responses.

Supply & Ethics

Massive numbers of animals were needed; vegetarians/religious groups faced conflict.

screens.title: Comparing Insulin Sources
screens.html:
🔑

Comparing Insulin Sources

Animal-Derived

Extracted from bovine/porcine sources.

Slower absorption rates.

Higher risk of cross-species contamination.

Synthetic (Humulin)

100% human amino acid sequence.

Produced in controlled lab vats.

Faster acting and more reliable dosing.

Key point

Humulin (100% human DNA sequence) was the first recombinant DNA drug approved by the FDA in 1982.

screens.title: KEY CONCEPT
screens.html:
KEY CONCEPT

Human Growth Hormone (hGH)

hGH is produced by the pituitary gland. Deficiencies lead to growth failure.

Before recombinant DNA, hGH was extracted from the pituitary glands of cadavers. This carried a terrifying risk: the transmission of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), a fatal brain disorder.

screens.title: Synthesising hGH
screens.html:
Synthesising hGH

Synthetic hGH (Somatropin) is produced using recombinant DNA in E. coli. Because it is not derived from human tissue, the risk of CJD is eliminated.

It allows children with pituitary dwarfism to reach an average height and maintains muscle/bone density in adults.

Synthetic hGH is safer than cadaver-derived hGH primarily because it is more potent.

Why is that?

b) It is safer because it removes the risk of transmitting infectious prions (CJD) found in human brain tissue.

screens.title: Managing Hypothyroidism
screens.html:
Managing Hypothyroidism

Hypothyroidism occurs when the thyroid gland is underactive, leading to a slow metabolism, fatigue, and weight gain.

Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of the hormone T₄. It is chemically identical to the thyroxine produced by your thyroid gland.

screens.title: How Levothyroxine Works
screens.html:
How Levothyroxine Works

Levothyroxine acts as a 'replacement' hormone. Once ingested, the body converts it into T₃, the active form of the hormone, restoring the body's metabolic balance.

screens.title: Manufacturing Scale
screens.html:
Manufacturing Scale

To produce these hormones at a global scale, scientists use bioreactors.

These are giant vats where temperature, pH, and nutrient levels are perfectly tuned to keep the recombinant bacteria multiplying and 'pumping out' the desired protein.

screens.title: The Quality of Life Impact
screens.html:
The Quality of Life Impact

Biotechnology doesn't just keep people alive; it allows them to thrive.

Stability: Consistent hormone levels.

Convenience: High-purity doses mean fewer side effects.

Longevity: Dramatic increase in life expectancy for diabetics.

screens.title: Economic and Social Benefits
screens.html:
Economic and Social Benefits

Lower Costs

Mass production in bacteria is cheaper than extracting from animal organs.

Reduced Hospitalisation

Better management of chronic conditions leads to fewer emergency admissions.

screens.title: Looking Ahead: Gene Therapy
screens.html:
🧠

Looking Ahead: Gene Therapy

While synthetic hormones treat the symptoms, gene therapy aims to cure the cause.

Instead of injecting insulin daily, could we insert a functional insulin gene directly into a patient's own cells?

Remember

Gene therapy uses a vector (like a virus) to deliver DNA into human cells, whereas recombinant DNA technology uses bacteria to make the protein outside the body.

screens.title: The ATAR Perspective
screens.html:
The ATAR Perspective

In exams, you may be asked to evaluate the impact of biotechnology on society.

Always link the biological process (recombinant DNA) to the human outcome (improved survival rates, economic productivity, and quality of life).

screens.title: Thinking Critically
screens.html:
Thinking Critically

If synthetic hormones are so effective, why is there still a massive push for gene therapy and stem cell research in treating endocrine disorders?

screens.title: Thinking Critically
screens.html:
Thinking Critically

You might have said...

Synthetic hormones are lifelong and do not cure the condition.

Gene therapy offers a potential one-time permanent fix.

Daily dosing burdens patients and risks compliance issues.

Cells manage biological feedback loops better than external drugs.

✅​

questions.title: Written practice
questions.prompt: Outline the production of a human hormone using recombinant DNA technology and explain why purification matters.
steps: Insert an appropriate hormone coding sequence into an expression vector and introduce it into suitable host cells.
Culture the selected cells and recover the hormone or precursor, including required processing.
Purify and test the product to remove contaminants and confirm its identity and activity before use.

bank.q: What is inserted into a production vector to make human insulin?
o: A suitable coding sequence for the insulin product
bank.why: A suitable coding sequence allows an engineered host to produce insulin or its precursor.

bank.q: What must happen before a manufactured hormone is used?
o: Direct injection of the bacterial culture
bank.why: The product must be purified and checked for identity, purity and biological activity.

bank.q: Why can human recombinant insulin be useful compared with animal insulin?
o: It provides a human product and scalable production
It is made without a coding sequence
bank.why: Recombinant production can supply a human product at scale; it does not remove the need for treatment or quality control.
